messages:
maya: Heads-up — we received a model bundle into the incoming bucket: s3://redwood-ml/incoming/zenith-2.0.tgz. Metadata attached but missing tokenizer sha256. Can someone validate provenance before we register it? :eyes:

ingest-bot: DELIVERY NOTICE: object=zenith-2.0.tgz size=4.6GB uploader=partner-ocm metadata=(manifest.json, receipt.sig). kms_key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKey/weightsKey

tariq: grabbing it now. I'll run checksum + unpack smoke tests. ETA ~10m.

zhen: quick checklist while tariq pulls: 1) weights sha256 2) tokenizer vocab hash 3) manifest signer verification 4) model card + license 5) registry slot created (dev-preview)

eli: if tokenizer hash is missing we shouldn't onboard into prod registry. We can create a temp registry entry with state=quarantine and comment why. Also note quantization experiments must reference original float32 artifact and quant config.

tariq: Ran local checks:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ml/incoming/zenith-2.0.tgz /tmp/ && sha256sum /tmp/zenith-2.0.tgz
# output: 3b9f3a7c2d...  zenith-2.0.tgz
mkdir /tmp/zenith && tar -xzvf /tmp/zenith-2.0.tgz -C /tmp/zenith
cat /tmp/zenith/tokenizer/vocab.txt | sha256sum
# output: MISSING (file not present)
```
Result: weights present and checksum matches partner receipt, tokenizer directory missing. manifest.json claims tokenizer.vocab_sha256 but entry is null.

maya: thanks. Partner notes said tokenizer shipped as a separate artifact to their registry. Can we ask for the tokenizer artifact and the signing key fingerprint? @zhen can you open a short intake ticket and mark priority=high for onboarding?

zhen: opening ticket: https://tracker.internal/ML-INTAKE-4217 — fields: source=partner-ocm, assets=[weights:sha256=3b9f3a7c..., tokenizer=null], initial_state=quarantine. Assigning to partner-eng for tokenizer delivery.

eli: for the quant experiments: when tokenizer arrives, run these steps in dev-preview cluster:
1) register float32 weights under registry name `zenith-2.0-f32` with provenance link to s3 and manifest
2) run `quantize --mode=int8 --calib=dynamic --seq-len=512` on a small eval set (5k samples) and store quant config as YAML in registry metadata
3) run our baseline evals (LLM-bench-lite) and diff against f32; alert if ROUGE/LLM-bench delta > 3% or latency regresses >15%

maya: also add KMS key fingerprint and signature verification steps to the registry entry: we need signer identity (x509 fingerprint) and the signature file `receipt.sig`. If signature verification fails, keep artifacts isolated.

tariq: pinged partner for tokenizer artifact + signer pubkey. They replied: "uploading tokenizer to s3://partner-temp/zenith-tokenizer-v1.zip, signer=0A:4B:...:FF". I will mirror it into our quarantine bucket when received and re-run checks.

zhen: updated intake ticket with partner-s3 path, expected ETA 4h. Adding checklist items for ops: duplicate-detection (compare vocab size & hash), license check, and storage class (GLACIER? no — must be STANDARD for active testing).

maya: perfect. Once tokenizer is in and checks pass, we can create the dev-preview registry entry and schedule quant smoke job. If anything looks off re: provenance or signature, escalate to security. :lock:

eli: note for the runbook — capture these artifacts in the provenance ledger: weights_sha256, tokenizer_sha256, manifest.sig, signer_fingerprint, registry_entry_id, and snapshot of eval metrics. Keep logs for 90 days.

ingest-bot: TICKET UPDATE: ML-INTAKE-4217 status=waiting_for_partner_assets (timestamp=1969876619)

maya: thanks team. low-chatter until partner confirms.
